neighbours.label: the negating prefix ' un' as its own token at the start of an adjective or adverb (unconditionally, unblemished, uncomplicated)
fire: The board agreed to accept the offer unconditionally after a short debate.
Critics found the new novel strangely unremarkable despite all the hype.
The hikers returned from the storm cold but completely unharmed.
Her answer was so unexpected that the whole room fell silent.
The contract leaves several key questions about payment unanswered.
For years the old mansion stood empty and unloved at the end of the lane.
The suspect remained calm and uncooperative throughout the interview.
Investors were unconvinced by the company's optimistic forecast.
quiet: The board agreed to accept the offer immediately after a short debate.
Critics found the new novel strangely moving despite all the hype.
The hikers returned from the storm cold but completely safe.
Her answer was so surprising that the whole room fell silent.
The contract leaves several key questions about payment open.
For years the old mansion stood empty and neglected at the end of the lane.
The suspect remained calm and silent throughout the interview.
Investors were skeptical of the company's optimistic forecast.

notes: ' un'/'un' are the commonest peak tokens (5 of 32); other top examples are endings (terminated, gone down). Near misses use the positive adjective without un-.
